newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swiss business draws up contingency plans for HK.
newsitem.headline: Swiss business draws up contingency plans for HK.

text.p: A business confidence survey of Swiss companies operating in Hong Kong showed most had drawn up contingency plans in case things go wrong in Hong Kong in the transition to China next year.

The survey, conducted by the Swiss Business Council of Hong Kong and analysed by Hong Kong-based Political & Economic Risk Consultancy Ltd, showed nearly all plan to stay beyond the handover and were upbeat about the medium term outlook.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over a century and a half, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.

Caution nevertheless prevails in the countdown period, the Business Confidence Survey of 80 companies showed, with only 36 percent of respondents replying were increasing investment spending in 1996, compared with 40 percent in 1995.
Eight percent said they would decrease investment spending this year, up from five percent last year.
"More than half the respondents said they had contingency plans in place in case the transition goes badly," the study concluded, but noted the sense of caution applied only to the short-term.
"There is a much greater sense of optimism expressed about the prospects for Hong Kong once the transition has actually taken place," it said.
Those who expressed pessimism about prospects for 1997 believe business will be back to normal by 1988 and 35 percent are upbeat about prospects for 1998.
"There is virtual consensus about one thing: Hong Kong's medium prospects are not bad," the survey concluded.
